main_text.p: sponsionem, systema Tychonis hic, addito schemate, inferere libet. Ipsius hypothesis hæc est (ut in schemate videre est) ponit Terram in universi centro quiescentem, & Solem cum toto systemate orbium cœlestium l. ♄♃♂♀☿☽, motu diurno circa eam velocissime actum ab oriente in occidentem, secundum circulum. s. b. a. e. qui est motus generalis omnium luminarium cœlestium: præter quem Planetarum unusquisque in Zodiaco . movetur motu proprio ab Occidente in Orientem, circa proprium centrum. Ita Sol movetur in ecliptica s. e. a. b, & singulis diebus fere gradum
main_text.notes: The diagram shows the Tychonic system: concentric orbits labelled with planetary symbols (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Sun, Venus, Mercury, Moon) around the Earth at centre, with the sphere of fixed stars outermost; its letters (β, α, ι, etc.) are not transcribed. Planetary symbols in the text are approximate. The final word "gradum" is cut off at the foot of the page and the last line is partly illegible.
